assumptions: The two redox partners are the two already-validated ORCA minima of the PMe3 model [Ni(SMe)2(PMe3)2]: the neutral (charge 0, multiplicity 1, orca-result-2f163213a49d1997) and the doublet cation (charge 1, multiplicity 2, orca-result-0ac07d4977dfbe94). Both carry 105 vibrational modes and near_zero_mode_count 0, and the host records both as valid.

The quartet partner is orca-result-ec426b8d2e3db9fe (charge 1, multiplicity 4, 105 modes, near_zero_mode_count 0). Its project artifact differs from the doublet's, but the host's own level summary for both is identical (def2-SVP, pbe0, d3bj, def2/j, cpcm, frequencies), and I verified solvent and model directly on all three logs, so the gap is a like-for-like comparison at one physical level.

The def2-TZVP re-evaluation is a fixed-geometry (def2-SVP) single-point correction on both partners, so it estimates the differential basis effect on the one-electron difference and does not include geometry relaxation at the larger basis.

The registered Fc+/Fc absolute reduction potential in acetonitrile (4.988 V, Namazian 2010, host-owned) is the correct reference for quoting this couple; the task's oxidant potentials (0.00, +0.27, +0.70 V) are the user's own shelf values and enter only as literals in the margin claims.

The three functional single points (PBE0, B3LYP, TPSSh) were all run at the PBE0 geometries, so their spread isolates the functional dependence of the ionisation energy and excludes geometry-relaxation differences between functionals.

The declared observable e-couple-vs-fc-pme3 is the model complex, not the user's real 2,6-dimethylbenzenethiolate/dmpe compound; model-to-real transfer is therefore reported as a limitation and is deliberately NOT inside this claim's uncertainty budget.
diagnostics: Declared basis-shift diagnostic: expected within +/-0.05 V, measured +0.0786 V. Diverged, and its stated failure_update_rule was applied, making the basis-corrected couple the delivery.

Refutation read on the basis comparison: the def2-SVP and def2-TZVP cation single points use different geometry artifacts, so I tested whether they are the same structure. Ni-S and Ni-P distances agree to 1.8e-5 angstrom and the D3BJ dispersion energies agree to 2e-9 Ha (-0.050751027 vs -0.050751025). No refutation: the shift is a pure basis effect.

Stationary-point character: near_zero_mode_count is 0 for all three minima under the 20 cm^-1 convention, consistent with the host's recorded_valid states and with previously delivered imaginary-mode counts of zero, so no saddle contaminates the thermochemistry.

Electronic-state identity re-read from the results themselves: neutral charge 0 multiplicity 1; doublet cation charge 1 multiplicity 2 with S-squared 0.7741 (ideal 0.75); quartet cation charge 1 multiplicity 4 with S-squared 3.7647 (ideal 3.75). Each surface is the state it is used as.

Entropy-treatment perturbation: Grimme qRRHO with a 100 cm^-1 cutoff moves the couple by only 0.0035 V (-0.4763 vs -0.4727 V), and the full electronic/RRHO/qRRHO spread is 0.0049 V, so the RRHO choice is not load-bearing.
Replication of the prior chain: the SVP RRHO couple reproduces the value three earlier goals delivered to 1e-10 V, so the correction I added is the only thing that moved.

Recorded divergences explained: gap-qrt-dbl-pme3 previously carried both 0.3502 and 0.2191 eV because the electronic-energy difference and the Gibbs difference were claimed under one id; both are now claimed under distinct state-explicit ids with their 0.1311 eV thermal term, whose dominant piece is the quartet's 0.1088 eV larger T*S. The e-couple-vs-fc-pme3 and oxidant-margin rows will diverge from prior goals by exactly the measured +0.0786 V basis correction, and uncertainty-e-couple-pme3 moves from 0.2012 to 0.1657 V because it is now composed of six named terms. The older dq-* rows pair equal-magnitude opposite-sign values (an oxidation-direction convention difference) and the spin_square rows pair a quartet value with a doublet value under one claim id; both are label collisions, and this cycle's ids are state-specific.
record.method_rationale: Both owed observables were re-derived from results already registered in this workspace, so this cycle consumed no engine call. The couple is the difference of harmonic-RRHO Gibbs free energies at 298.15 K and 1 atm of the validated neutral and doublet-cation minima (PBE0-D3BJ/def2-SVP, CPCM acetonitrile), written in reduction order so no sign flip of mine enters the arithmetic, converted by gibbs_to_redox_potential with the electron count derived as the difference of the two states' own charge selectors (n = 1), and referenced by ordinary subtraction against the registered Fc+/Fc constant, so the reference stays visible. That reproduces the workspace's def2-SVP value exactly (-0.472742 V, agreeing with prior goals to 1e-10 V). The declared diagnostic was then evaluated rather than assumed: re-evaluating both partners at def2-TZVP on their own def2-SVP geometries moves the ionisation free energy from 4.5094 to 4.5880 eV, a shift of +0.0786 V. That exceeds the 0.05 V deadband, so the diagnostic's own failure_update_rule fires and the basis-corrected couple, -0.3941 V, is the delivery; the uncorrected SVP value is still claimed separately. The quartet-minus-doublet gap is the difference of the two relaxed cations' RRHO Gibbs energies, 0.2191 eV, with the electronic-energy difference (0.3502 eV) and their 0.1311 eV thermal term claimed alongside it, which resolves the recorded divergence under that claim id as definitional rather than numerical. The uncertainty is composed of six named terms, three of them measured from receipts containing no model-authored number, combined in quadrature to 0.1657 V; the conservative linear sum, 0.2649 V, is claimed as its own number so a reader can prefer it.
uncertainties: Functional choice dominates: PBE0, B3LYP and TPSSh span 0.1470 V at common def2-SVP geometries, and the delivered PBE0 value sits at the positive edge of the basis-corrected set, 0.1528 V from its most negative member. A reader who prefers a functional midpoint would quote about -0.49 V, still inside the stated interval.

Basis incompleteness beyond def2-TZVP is estimated, not measured: I took one third of the measured SVP-to-TZVP step (0.0262 V). A def2-QZVP pair would replace that estimate with a measurement at the cost of two engine calls.

The Fc+/Fc absolute potential in acetonitrile is a single registered determination (4.988 V); other published determinations differ by up to about 0.05 V, and that shift moves this couple one-for-one.

CPCM systematic error on a +1/0 couple is taken as 0.03 V. Both partners are the same molecule differing by one electron and the reference couple is also +1/0, so much of the continuum error should cancel, but nothing here measures the residual.

The combined 0.1657 V is a quadrature of six terms, two of which (Fc reference, CPCM) are asserted and one of which (basis residual) uses my one-third estimator; the host records the total as inferred and not evidence-backed, which is the honest label.

Transfer to the user's real compound is unbounded here. The observable is the SMe/PMe3 model; this workspace measures +0.196 V for the PH3-to-PMe3 substitution alone, so ligand identity moves this couple by roughly 0.2 V per substantial donor change, and replacing an alkyl thiolate with a 2,6-dimethylbenzenethiolate (a weaker donor) should shift it positive. The real compound's couple may therefore be meaningfully less negative than -0.39 V.

The doublet-quartet gap carries an unquantified functional component: no B3LYP or TPSSh quartet minimum exists in this workspace. Its measured thermal sensitivity alone is 0.1311 eV, comparable to the gap itself (0.2191 eV), so the gap should be read as 'doublet ground state, quartet within a few kT at 298 K' rather than as a precise number.

An earlier pass at these expressions negated the oxidation free energy with a scale factor of -1; the host correctly treated those receipts as model-authored and refused them as measured evidence. They were rebuilt in reduction order and superseded; the values are numerically identical.

result.method_rationale: Both owed observables were re-derived from results already registered in this workspace, so this cycle consumed no engine call. The couple is the difference of harmonic-RRHO Gibbs free energies at 298.15 K and 1 atm of the validated neutral and doublet-cation minima (PBE0-D3BJ/def2-SVP, CPCM acetonitrile), written in reduction order so no sign flip of mine enters the arithmetic, converted by gibbs_to_redox_potential with the electron count derived as the difference of the two states' own charge selectors (n = 1), and referenced by ordinary subtraction against the registered Fc+/Fc constant, so the reference stays visible. That reproduces the workspace's def2-SVP value exactly (-0.472742 V, agreeing with prior goals to 1e-10 V). The declared diagnostic was then evaluated rather than assumed: re-evaluating both partners at def2-TZVP on their own def2-SVP geometries moves the ionisation free energy from 4.5094 to 4.5880 eV, a shift of +0.0786 V. That exceeds the 0.05 V deadband, so the diagnostic's own failure_update_rule fires and the basis-corrected couple, -0.3941 V, is the delivery; the uncorrected SVP value is still claimed separately. The quartet-minus-doublet gap is the difference of the two relaxed cations' RRHO Gibbs energies, 0.2191 eV, with the electronic-energy difference (0.3502 eV) and their 0.1311 eV thermal term claimed alongside it, which resolves the recorded divergence under that claim id as definitional rather than numerical. The uncertainty is composed of six named terms, three of them measured from receipts containing no model-authored number, combined in quadrature to 0.1657 V; the conservative linear sum, 0.2649 V, is claimed as its own number so a reader can prefer it.
uncertainties: Functional choice dominates: PBE0, B3LYP and TPSSh span 0.1470 V at common def2-SVP geometries, and the delivered PBE0 value sits at the positive edge of the basis-corrected set, 0.1528 V from its most negative member. A reader who prefers a functional midpoint would quote about -0.49 V, still inside the stated interval.

Basis incompleteness beyond def2-TZVP is estimated, not measured: I took one third of the measured SVP-to-TZVP step (0.0262 V). A def2-QZVP pair would replace that estimate with a measurement at the cost of two engine calls.

The Fc+/Fc absolute potential in acetonitrile is a single registered determination (4.988 V); other published determinations differ by up to about 0.05 V, and that shift moves this couple one-for-one.

CPCM systematic error on a +1/0 couple is taken as 0.03 V. Both partners are the same molecule differing by one electron and the reference couple is also +1/0, so much of the continuum error should cancel, but nothing here measures the residual.

The combined 0.1657 V is a quadrature of six terms, two of which (Fc reference, CPCM) are asserted and one of which (basis residual) uses my one-third estimator; the host records the total as inferred and not evidence-backed, which is the honest label.

Transfer to the user's real compound is unbounded here. The observable is the SMe/PMe3 model; this workspace measures +0.196 V for the PH3-to-PMe3 substitution alone, so ligand identity moves this couple by roughly 0.2 V per substantial donor change, and replacing an alkyl thiolate with a 2,6-dimethylbenzenethiolate (a weaker donor) should shift it positive. The real compound's couple may therefore be meaningfully less negative than -0.39 V.

The doublet-quartet gap carries an unquantified functional component: no B3LYP or TPSSh quartet minimum exists in this workspace. Its measured thermal sensitivity alone is 0.1311 eV, comparable to the gap itself (0.2191 eV), so the gap should be read as 'doublet ground state, quartet within a few kT at 298 K' rather than as a precise number.
